title: auth: unify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS and request signing (OpenAI compat)
author: Maya Thompson
body: This PR standardizes header semantics across the API surface with focus on project/org key handling, scoped tokens, CORS rules for browser clients, and request signing/nonce support. Motivation: inconsistent header parsing across the OpenAI-compat layer and native API caused subtle auth bypasses and confusing developer experience for project-scoped tokens and browser-based app usage. This change unifies behavior so that: 1) Authorization remains 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' for both Redwood-native and OpenAI-compat requests. 2) Project-scoped tokens must include a matching 'X-Redwood-Project' header (project ID) or an explicit 'Redwood-Project' query param for legacy clients; otherwise the request is rejected with 401. 3) Organization keys (org_) are allowed to omit project header and may route by default project mapping; admin APIs still require explicit 'X-Redwood-Org' when performing org-scoped operations. 4) Introduces 'X-Redwood-Nonce' header to support replay protection for request signing flows; when 'X-Redwood-Signature' ('HMAC-SHA256') is supplied the nonce is required and validated for freshness/unique windows. 5) CORS: preflight now exposes and allows Authorization, X-Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Project, and X-Redwood-Signature headers; we tightened allowed origins for public endpoints and documented recommended browser patterns for delegated keys. 6) OpenAI compatibility layer: the adapter continues to accept OpenAI-style keys but now enforces the same project/org header semantics and maps 'OpenAI-Organization' header into 'X-Redwood-Org' for parity. 7) Streaming and function-calling paths were audited to ensure header propagation through the proxy and to downstream runtime workers; fixes included passing the project header in the initial handshake to prevent incorrect KV-cache isolation. The PR includes code changes (auth gateway, openai_compat adapter, streaming proxy), unit and integration tests, and updated docs/examples in SDKs. Checklist: - auth gateway parsing + validation implemented - CORS policy updates + e2e browser test - nonce/signature validation with idempotency window - openai-compat header mapping - SDK docs + examples updated - changelog entry The description below summarizes commits, changed files, CI checks, and review discussion.
commits: feat(auth): add project/org header parsing and validation
fix(auth): require X-Redwood-Nonce when signature present
test(cors): add e2e preflight tests for custom headers
docs: auth header semantics + sdk examples
review_comments: Alexei Romanov: Can we make the X-Redwood-Project header optional for project-scoped tokens if the token includes project claim? Response: Maya Thompson: yes -- implementation accepts project claim in token but requires header when token is ambiguous or when org token is used; added explicit checks and tests.

Priya Desai: Nonce window and replay table lookups could be a performance hotspot at high QPS; have you considered a bloom filter fallback? Response: Maya Thompson: we added an in-memory LRU + probabilistic dedupe for high-throughput paths and fall back to datastore for long-term uniqueness; documented tradeoffs in comments.

Jordan Kim: OpenAI compat mapping may unintentionally expose org IDs; ensure we don't leak internal mapping in error messages. Response: Maya Thompson: scrubbed error messages and added tests to assert no org id in 4xx bodies; logs still contain IDs under SENSITIVE log level only.
release_notes:
- Unified authorization header semantics: project vs org keys
- Browser CORS: Authorization, X-Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Project allowed in preflight
- Added X-Redwood-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signature support for request signing
- OpenAI-compat layer enforces same header rules and maps OpenAI-Organization
- SDK docs updated with examples and guidance for scoped tokens
